current.text: In preseason his rebound rate, assist rate and usage rate are all down.
The Bulls are feeding usage to rookie Caleb Wilson in preseason.
Experts are worried about his preseason. It is unclear how new coach Tiago Splitter will use him.
He is in the projected starting five with Norman Powell, Matas Buzelis, Caleb Wilson and Nick Claxton.

Experts disagree on his usage. Some say the exits of Nikola Vucevic and Coby White free up touches and he will be the offensive hub. Others expect his usage to drop, with Norman Powell possibly leading the team.
Experts project about 33 to 34 minutes and around 10 assists per game.
Experts value him as a second round pick in category leagues, fine around picks 18 to 25 but not earlier. ESPN's pick 11 is too high.
In one mock auction he went for 29 USD. The expert bid up to 24 USD and passed, calling 29 USD no bargain.
His shooting dropped last season, including an odd fall in free throw percentage. Experts are unsure whether it bounces back.
He dealt with ankle injuries last season.
He is the only Bulls player paid over 20 million USD per year and faces the most pressure if the season goes badly.
The Bulls are expected to be a bad team, around 32 wins. They lack shooting, and a lineup with Claxton, Wilson and Giddey has poor spacing.
The Bulls should play a fast, up-tempo transition style.
Chicago plays 10 games in our fantasy playoff weeks (3-3-4) and has 15 back-to-backs, one below the maximum. The first 20 games are a tough stretch.

durable.text: He is a reliable source of points, rebounds and assists, with possible double digit assists. Rebounding and transition play are strengths.
Assists are a league outlier, and his rebounds are far above other guards.
Turnovers are a league outlier on the weak side. He is a ball-dominant passer who needs to cut them.
Experts disagree on his usage profile. One calls him a low usage player whose variance comes from percentages and steals. Another calls him a high-usage passer.
He shot about 37% and 36.5% from three over the last two seasons, on low volume.
Availability is a concern. He needs to play over 60 to 65 games.
Experts rate him higher in points leagues than in category leagues, so points-based rankings overrate him for us.

note: He is a top assist source with guard-leading rebounds, but he costs you in turnovers and gives slightly below-average shooting percentages. That makes him a natural fit for punt TO builds. Yahoo prices him at 37 USD, ESPN's value is only 20 USD (average cost 32.6), he went for 31 USD in our league last season and 29 USD in a mock auction. With experts worried about his preseason role and calling him a category-league second rounder, about 28 to 32 USD is fair and the full Yahoo price is too much. Early in the season, check his usage and assist rates under Splitter next to Powell and Wilson, and whether his FT% recovers toward 78%.
